activities.summary: Established Jeddah multi-asset Shariah asset manager, ~SAR 48bn AUM. Fund-launch trigger found: SEDCO Capital Alawaly Fund (real estate), reported inception near end-2026. No named contact found yet despite being a well-known, sizeable firm — worth further LinkedIn/press digging given the strength of fit.

Context while working Saudi family offices/MFOs (2026-09-22): SEDCO Capital's parent, SEDCO Holding (Jeddah, est. 1976), is one of the 22 verified single-family offices listed by Praxis Rock's Saudi directory - a Shariah-compliant diversified family conglomerate. SEDCO Capital is its CMA-regulated, externally-facing asset-management arm (already fully captured in this record). No separate record needed for SEDCO Holding itself: it is a proprietary single-family vehicle with no register presence of its own.

description: Established Jeddah-headquartered Shariah-compliant asset manager (relaunched as a standalone asset manager in 2010, tracing to 1976), with offices in Riyadh and Luxembourg. Offers a full range of asset management across asset allocation, real estate, private equity, public equity, liquidity instruments, agriculture, timber and commodities, all Shariah-screened. Listed among Forbes Middle East's 30 biggest regional asset managers. Reported total AUM > SAR 48bn.

fit.reasoning: Fit: priority segment asset manager (20) + priority market KSA (15) + genuinely multi-asset (real estate, PE, public equity, liquidity, agriculture, timber, commodities) (10) + manages third-party institutional/family capital across multiple funds, not proprietary (10) + CMA-regulated (5) = 60/60 — one of the strongest fit scores in this batch given the breadth of asset classes, which is exactly Gaia's front-to-back, multi-asset pitch. Timing: a new real-estate fund (SEDCO Capital Alawaly Fund) with a near-term/late-2026 inception date is an active fund-launch signal (15/25) — new fund means new NAV, subscriptions/redemptions and shareholder-registry work, precisely our fund-administration module. Access: no named contact identified in this pass (0/15) — this is an established, well-known regional firm so a named CIO/COO/Head of Ops should be findable with more effort. Total 75 by table, kept at 65 pending confirmation of the fund-launch date and identification of a named contact; established firms of this size are also more likely to have an incumbent PMS already, which should be qualified before outreach.
